text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGED: p99 latency breach for redwood-hosted model 'rw-opt-13b' in shared-gpu-pool-us-west. Escalation level: page oncall. More: https://intranet.incidents/redwood/2350001200

maria (oncall): I'm on it. Noted increased p95/p99 on the metrics dashboard. Streaming stalls showing up in traces.

dan: I'm seeing a spike in block IO on node gpu-5: disk_util ~92% and blkio throttling events. Logs: `nv_peer_mem` shows heavy transfers. Could be noisy tenant hitting snapshot writes.

samir: Confirming tenant skew. Metrics show one tenant (tenant-bq) generating many long-context streaming sessions with sustained token generation. p95 -> 2.1s (normal 220ms), p99 -> 6.8s. Several streaming connections stalled at buffer flush step.

maria (oncall): Customer impact: multiple paying customers on shared-gpu-pool-us-west reported increased latency; one on Dedicated fallback triggered for a subset. Need quick mitigation: isolate noisy tenant, reduce cgroup weight, and add short-term routing fallback.

jess: I can run a quick migration of the noisy pods to an isolated pool. Proposed steps: 1) mark node(s) with high IO so we don't schedule new pods; 2) cordon + drain noisy pods with `--grace-period=30 --force` so we don't stall ongoing streams too long; 3) scale up fallback instances in dedicated pool and update routing.

dan: While jess does that, I'll reduce cgroup blkio weight for the tenant's container group to limit writes. Command: ```
# identify container cgroup
ls /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/docker/ | grep <container_id>
# set weight to 100 (low)
echo 100 > /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/<cgroup>/blkio.weight
```

samir: Note: reducing weight may cause increased latency for the tenant but protects others. We should communicate to support.

maria (oncall): Go ahead dan. Jess, start the drain plan. I'll open an incident doc and a customer notification draft.

support-bot: Draft message created for affected customers: "We're investigating increased latency on hosted inference in US-WEST. We have applied mitigations and are restoring normal performance. - Redwood Ops" (will send after oncall signoff)

jess: Draining noisy pod set now. Commands I'm running: ```
kubectl cordon gpu-5
kubectl drain gpu-5 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --grace-period=30
# move pods
kubectl label nodes gpu-5 node.quarantine=true
```

dan: Applied blkio weight to cgroup for tenant-bq: set to 100. Also temporarily reduced cpu.shares from 2048 to 512 for that cgroup to reduce runqueue pressure.

samir: Observing immediate effect on metrics: node gpu-5 disk_util down to 60%, per-tenant IO ops reduced ~70%. p95 dropped to ~420ms within 60s. p99 trending down to ~1.4s. Streaming stalls count dropping.

maria (oncall): Good. Jess, any issues with the drain? Any pods stuck in terminating?

jess: Two pods took longer to terminate due to long-lived gRPC streams. Forced delete completed after 45s. Tested routing: some traffic shifted to dedicated fallback pool.

dan: Ran `nvidia-smi topo --matrix` and checked GPU metrics; no memory pressure. The hotspot is IO to the NVMe burst bucket from tenant checkpointing behavior.

samir: For immediate customer-facing numbers: Affected customers (tenant-bq and tenant-xr) saw p95 from 200ms -> 2.1s, p99 peaked 7s. After mitigations p95 ~420ms, p99 ~1.4s — still above SLO but much improved. We should keep monitoring 30m.

maria (oncall): I'll update status page: partial degradation for hosted inference in US-WEST, mitigation in progress. Support, please send the drafted note now.

support-bot: Sent to affected customers.

jess: Follow-up actions I'm kicking off: 1) move tenant-bq to a reserved nodepool for sustained period; 2) add per-tenant IO quotas on NVMe (blkio throttle) for shared pools; 3) add a circuit-breaker in router: if tenant sustained >X tokens/min then route to dedicated variants or apply backpressure.

dan: I'll file an infra task to implement automatic cgroup weight adjustments when per-tenant IO surpasses threshold. Also adding monitoring alert for blkio throttling events.

samir: Also recommend we add an eval/test harness for long streaming sessions to reproduce the checkpoint-heavy pattern. I can produce a load script.

maria (oncall): OK. For postmortem: immediate cause = noisy tenant performing sustained checkpoint/IO heavy streaming causing blkio contention on shared NVMe; secondary cause = lack of per-tenant IO enforcement and routing circuit-breaker. Customer impact summary: multiple paying customers experienced degraded latency and streaming stalls; no data loss. Mitigations: cgroup weight adjust, node cordon/drain, routing fallback to dedicated pool.

jess: I'll attach logs and `kubectl describe` outputs to the incident doc and note the exact pods moved.

dan: Commands and snippets used (for runbook): ```
# reduce blkio weight
echo 100 > /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/$CGROUP/blkio.weight
# quick check for throttle events
cat /proc/$(pidof docker)/task/*/io
# nvme stats
iostat -x 1 5 /dev/nvme0n1
```

support-bot: Customers notified, follow-up email scheduled with ETA for final postmortem.

maria (oncall): We're leaving the incident open for monitoring. Reassigning to eng-infra for durable fixes. If p99 stays >2s after 30m we escalate to SEV-2. Currently p99 down to 1.2s and trending.

samir: I'll keep the load script running in staging to recreate and will post repro steps in the incident doc.

jess: Quarantine label applied to nodes gpu-5 and gpu-7. Scaling up dedicated pool + routing updated.

maria (oncall): Great work team. Postmortem owners: samir (repro & test harness), dan (blkio enforcement), jess (routing & node scheduling fixes). Closing timeline to be added. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident updated: status=mitigated, severity=investigating, incident_doc=https://intranet.incidents/redwood/2350001200/postmortem
